inline_text:
## Background

Each row in the [[use case inventory](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration/blob/main/workstreams/critical-use-cases/use-case-inventory.md)](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration/blob/main/workstreams/critical-use-cases/use-case-inventory.md) cites supporting evidence in the Notes column: vendor product pages and primary announcements that confirm a production deployment. Each citation carries a date (publication date or "retrieved" date).

These sources go stale. Vendors rename products, restructure their sites, get acquired, or shut down. When a citation breaks, the row loses its evidence, and the evidentiary standard (at least one verified, publicly accessible citation per use case) is no longer met.

This is tracked as a known gap in the schema (link rot and ephemeral sources). Manual re-verification does not scale, so this issue proposes automation.

## Goal

Automatically check every link in the Notes column and report any that no longer resolve.

**Acceptance criteria**
- A script or workflow extracts every URL from the Notes column of `use-case-inventory.md`
- Each URL is requested and its result recorded (resolves, redirects, 404, timeout, blocked)
- Failures are reported in a form a maintainer can act on: use case name, URL, and failure type
- Redirects are flagged separately from hard failures, since a redirect often signals a renamed or moved product page
- The check can run on demand and on a recurring schedule (for example, a scheduled GitHub Action)

## Stretch goal

Confirm that a link which still resolves still contains the supporting information.

A page can stay live while its content changes, so a 200 response does not prove the citation still supports the claim in the row. Possible approaches to evaluate:
- Check the page for the vendor or product name cited in the row
- Compare against a stored snapshot or content hash from the original retrieval and flag significant changes
- Use an LLM-assisted check that asks whether the page still supports the classification or deployment claim made in the row (needs a design for cost, false positives, and human review of results)

## Considerations

- Some vendor sites block automated requests or return 403 to bots. These should be reported as "unverifiable by script" rather than as broken, so a human can check them.
- Rate limiting: spread requests out and respect robots.txt where applicable.
- Output should feed back into the workflow already described in the schema: failures become GitHub issues or a report on the PR, and are fixed by updating the citation per the evidentiary standard.
- The "retrieved" date convention could be updated automatically when a link is re-verified, but that should be a separate decision.

## Out of scope

- Judging whether a replacement source meets the evidentiary standard (this stays a human review)
- Verifying the classification values themselves

## Related

- Evidentiary standard (`README.md`)
